linkedin.text:
Take a team out of a meeting room and put them somewhere with real altitude, and the conversation changes within a day. It is not mysticism. It is that nothing up there looks like work.

This is the High Atlas above Marrakesh, from a programme we produced. Snow on the ridge, an hour and a half from a warm city.

Mountain days are the highest-variance item in any itinerary. The weather decides, not you. Roads close. Cloud sits on the pass and the view your whole day was built around simply is not there. So the rule we work to is that a mountain day must be worth doing in bad conditions too — a lunch, a hosted visit, something indoors that stands on its own. If the day only works in sunshine, it is not a plan.

Want altitude in your 2026 programme? Let's build the version that survives bad weather.
